title: Trump Announces 'Economic D-Day' Against Iran, Warns Countries Against Providing Financial Support To Tehran
text:

US President Donald Trump announced what he termed an "Economic D-Day" against Iran yesterday (19 August), warning that any nation providing financial support to Tehran will face severe consequences.
The dramatic escalation came after a 60-day window to negotiate a peace deal with Iran expired on Monday without progress.
Writing on Truth Social, Trump declared he was launching the "most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country", describing the measures as "economic warfare and isolation on an unprecedented scale".
The US President specifically targeted countries allowing their financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities to assist Iran.
"Oil smuggling, swap lines, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries, front companies — it all needs to stop now. You know who you are," Trump wrote, in a pointed message apparently directed at China, Russia and Gulf states.
The announcement follows his administration's Operation Economic Fury campaign launched in April, which has already imposed sweeping sanctions on Iran's oil, shipping and financial sectors.
The timing of Trump's statement coincided with the United Arab Emirates' announcement yesterday that it was suspending economic ties with Iran following alleged ballistic missile attacks. Tehran rejected the accusations, describing the incident as an Israeli "false-flag operation".
Analysts suggest the new measures could include secondary sanctions targeting Chinese refineries still purchasing Iranian oil, though experts note Iran has developed sophisticated smuggling routes since Trump withdrew from the 2015 nuclear deal.
Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency responded that the country had "become very skilled" at circumventing such restrictions.
